outcome: The conjecture remains open in general, but the effective bound m in Fujita's freeness conjecture (K_M ⊗ L^⊗m globally generated for m ≥ dim+1) moved twice inside the window: a 2024 preprint claiming a full solution via analytic adjoint ideal sheaves was withdrawn after a flaw was found, and a September 2026 preprint by Jingjun Han claims a linear bound m ≥ ⌈1.776n⌉, improving on the previously best-known n·log(log n) bound.
summary: The triage's three finds check out but need care in dating and scope. (1) Ghidelli–Lacini's n·log(log n) bound was first posted to arXiv as 2107.11705 in July 2021 — well before the 26 Jan 2024 frozen revision — and only its Proceedings of the LMS journal version appeared in 2024; per §6.3 the event dates to the first written argument (2021), so this is open_stale and not a change in the window, despite the journal DOI carrying a 2024 date. (2) arXiv:2411.07129 (Tsz On Mario Chan, Nov 2024) claimed a full solution to the freeness conjecture using an extension theorem with analytic adjoint ideal sheaves; it was withdrawn after Professor S. Helmke identified a flaw in the construction of a local holomorphic section on p.31 that fails to preserve the required vanishing order under extension (illustrated with an {xy=z^2}-type counterexample to the construction). This is a genuine in-window event: an AI-free claim, announced and retracted, coded progress/incident dated to the November 2024 posting. (3) arXiv:2609.01574 (Jingjun Han, posted 1 Sep 2026, v2 on 11 Sep 2026) claims a linear bound m ≥ ⌈C₀n⌉ with C₀≈1.7763, a substantial improvement over the log-log bound, obtained via a new estimate for the multiplicity of a minimal log-canonical center; the paper is only three weeks old as of the check date and has not yet been digested by experts beyond an algebraic-geometry seminar presentation at the University of Michigan announcing it as 'after Jingjun Han' — not yet a vetted result. I read the full PDF (via fetch) and found no acknowledgement of any AI, machine-learning or language-model tool in the research, and none in the withdrawn Chan preprint either. The conjecture itself (full generality, all dimensions) remains open; the freeness conjecture is proved through dimension 5 (Ye–Zhu 2020, before the window) and the very-ampleness conjecture through dimension 2. No AI involvement was found anywhere in the trail. Status is coded progress because the best-known effective bound on an open conjecture moved (twice, net downward) within the window, with one intervening incident; no case of the conjecture was fully resolved.
competing_reading: One could argue the Han preprint, being unreviewed and only weeks old, should not yet count as 'progress' at all and the record should default to open/no_change_found — but §3.1 says size is not the test and a bound that moved counts, so I keep it as progress/claimed-bound territory rather than discounting it. Separately, one could read the PLMS 2024 publication as the operative event date since journal acceptance is itself a form of expert digestion of a result that was still informally circulating — but §6.3 explicitly instructs dating by first written argument, so I did not.
what_would_settle_it: Expert digestion (a referee report, a survey, or a blog treatment by an algebraic geometer) confirming or refuting Han's linear-bound argument, and confirmation of whether the paper has since been withdrawn or revised further.
